text:
olivia: Heads up — we just got a cluster of SSO auth failures across multiple tenants. 6 distinct user accounts tried to sign in from different countries over ~8 minutes. MFA pushes are failing and a few accounts are hitting lockout thresholds. seeing rapid session churn too. :rotating_light:
AuthBot: alert_id=auth-7621 severity=high
  pattern=geo-churn | distinct_users=6 | window=8m | actions=failed_pushes, lockouts
  sample_log: user=alice@example.com ip=89.45.12.34 geo=ES device=chrome-1234 result=push_timeout
raj: can someone run quick triage — confirm whether these are service accounts or human users? if humans we should avoid org-wide revokes unless containment needed.
maria: checking. initial hits look like normal user agents but inconsistent device ids. i'm running a refresh-token-scan now against those uids.
thomas: before mass action — what's the blast radius if we revoke refresh tokens for those 6 users? can we do per-user session revocation?
olivia: blast radius low if we target the 6. but there are 18 auth attempts clustered on a small set of IPs — could be a credential-stuffing tool rotating proxies. recommending immediate per-user refresh-token revoke + block IPs at WAF.
jen: i'll draft customer support note in case any of those users contact us. short template: "we detected abnormal sign-in attempts and temporarily revoked active sessions — if you were locked out follow link to reset". any legal to loop in?
raj: agree per-user revoke first. run these commands (admin CLI):
```
# revoke refresh tokens for user IDs
redwood-admin sessions revoke --user alice@example.com --reason "suspicious geo-churn"
redwood-admin sessions revoke --user bob@example.com --user charlie@example.com
```
# block IPs in WAF (example)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $WAF_API" https://waf.internal/blocks -d '{"ip":"89.45.12.34","reason":"sso-geo-churn"}'
```
AuthBot: enrichment: first_seen=2026-03-20T09:12:41Z, related_alerts=auth-7619,auth-7620, geos=[ES,UA,BR,US,DE,NG], user_types=[human,human,svc,human,human,human]
maria: running KMS audit for any recent unusual key usage tied to service accounts. nothing suspicious so far but will post results in 10m.
sre-oncall: if we revoke sessions we should ensure session store eviction completes before pushing any broader policy. I'll watch the cache invalidation queue.
thomas: note — don't rotate customer-facing KMS keys unless we have evidence of compromise. we can rotate internal service account keys if needed.
olivia: containment steps agreed: 1) revoke refresh tokens for the 6 users 2) block the top 3 suspicious IPs in WAF 3) add a temporary stricter push backoff policy for org (reduce retries to avoid MFA fatigue) 4) enable additional audit logging for SSO assertion headers and device fingerprints for next 48h
jen: communications: draft sent to support triage, cc: legal & trust. suggested user-facing blurb saved in #support-templates.
raj: post-action: create Jira SECURITY-INC-8989, assign to sec-ops, attach logs and list of revoked sessions. schedule 1h postmortem tomorrow at 11am PT.
maria: KMS audit finished: last key usage from suspicious IPs was >7 days ago and by infra deploy account. no active signs of key compromise.
AuthBot: update: blocked_ips=89.45.12.34,203.0.113.5,45.77.9.101 | revoked_sessions=6 | jira=SECURITY-INC-8989
olivia: good. please monitor for login retries and escalation to account lockout alerts. if we see new geos or increase in attempts, we'll escalate to org-wide rate limit. :lock:
thomas: small follow-up — add an eval prompt set to detect odd device-id toggles (session_device_id changing >3x in 5m) and tie to alert threshold.
sre-oncall: watching cache invalidation. will confirm when all sessions are evicted (ETA ~2m).
jen: support ready with message templates, will push to agents once we confirm user unlock flow.
olivia: thanks all. summary will go into the incident doc page and i'll own the postmortem runbook. :white_check_mark:
